7: {"id": "codex-51152", "titulo": "app-server rejects every turn with "invalid cwd" once the daemon's own working directory is deleted, even when the request cwd is absolute", "texto": "## What happens

The shared app-server daemon starts with the working directory of the first `codex` invocation that spawns it. If that directory is later deleted (a removed git worktree, for example), every new `turn/start` on that daemon fails:

```
turn/start failed: invalid cwd: No such file or directory (os error 2) (code -32600)
```

This happens even though the turn's own `cwd` is an absolute path to a directory that exists. Every TUI attached to the daemon is affected until the daemon restarts. `codex resume <thread> --no-daemon` works around it for one session.

## Why

`resolve_request_cwd` (codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors.rs:629, rust-v0.160.0) resolves the request cwd with `AbsolutePathBuf::relative_to_current_dir`:

```rust
fn resolve_request_cwd(cwd: Option<PathBuf>) -> Result<Option<AbsolutePathBuf>, JSONRPCErrorError> {
    cwd.map(|cwd| {
        AbsolutePathBuf::relative_to_current_dir(path_utils::normalize_for_native_workdir(cwd))
            .map_err(|err| invalid_request(format!("invalid cwd: {err}")))
    })
    .transpose()
}
```

`relative_to_current_dir` (codex-rs/utils/absolute-path/src/lib.rs:87) calls `std::env::current_dir()?` unconditionally, before it looks at whether `path` is already absolute:

```rust
pub fn relative_to_current_dir<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P) -> std::io::Result<Self> {
    Ok(Self::resolve_path_against_base(
        path,
        std::env::current_dir()?,
    ))
}
```

On Linux, `getcwd` fails with ENOENT when the process's cwd has been unlinked. So an absolute request path is rejected because of the daemon's own cwd, which the path does not depend on. The same call is used for `turn/start` (turn_processor.rs:621, :928) and thread resume (thread_processor.rs:3877).

## Reproduce

8: {"id": "codex-51153", "titulo": "Daemon bootstrap reports success while its updater exits with SUN_LEN under a deep CODEX_HOME (Linux)", "texto": "## Behaviour

On Linux with codex-cli 0.160.0, `app-server daemon bootstrap` successfully starts the managed app-server and records a daemon-updater PID, but the updater immediately exits when its Unix socket path exceeds the platform address limit. Its stderr contains `Error: path must be shorter than SUN_LEN`, and `daemon-updater.sock` never appears. The serving daemon survives, so an immediate PID-file check can incorrectly suggest that auto-update is working.

Observed in a private HOME under a pytest directory on 2026-10-03. No production daemon was stopped or restarted. The fixture's updater socket was longer than Linux's 108-byte Unix-address field. A short private HOME under disk TMPDIR produces a 99-byte updater address and is the proposed fixture workaround.

## Source

The updater binds its manual-update listener directly to `manual_update_socket_path()` in [update_loop.rs:118–128](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.160.0/codex-rs/app-server-daemon/src/update_loop.rs#L118).

The existing [deep control-socket path report](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/27765) describes daemon-client control addresses in 0.137/0.139 on macOS. This reproduction concerns the updater's separate socket in 0.160.0 on Linux; the app-server control socket itself works through its existing long-path fallback.

1. Create a private HOME on disk with a long absolute path. Set `CODEX_HOME` to its `.codex` directory. Choose the length so `$CODEX_HOME/app-server-daemon/daemon-updater.sock` exceeds 108 bytes.

10: {"id": "codex-51201", "titulo": "Managed daemon auto-update restart kills in-flight turns without a terminal event and reloads threads with default permissions instead of Full access (0.160.0 → 0.160.1, macOS)", "texto": "### What happened

macOS (arm64), managed app-server daemon with its own `CODEX_HOME`, several long-running desktop-app threads set to **Full access** (`permission_profile` type `disabled`, approval `never`).

1. The daemon's update loop installed **0.160.1** over **0.160.0**, and a minute later restarted the app-server.
2. Four threads had turns in progress. Each of those turns simply stops in its rollout: no `task_complete`, no `turn_aborted`, no error event. Nothing tells the thread (or the user) the turn was killed.
3. The restarted app-server emitted `thread_settings_applied` for each thread with `permission_profile` type `managed` and a `restricted` filesystem (workspace and tmp writable, no network), instead of the `disabled` profile the threads had before the restart.
4. The next turn on such a thread (started with `codex queue --thread …`) ran under that sandbox: no network, `.git` not writable. The agent could not reach anything outside the machine, including to ask for help. Nothing in the thread showed that its permissions had changed.

### Expected

- A daemon update does not restart the app-server under running turns (drain or hand off first), or at minimum records a terminal event with a reason on each interrupted turn.
- A thread's permission settings survive an app-server restart; a reloaded thread keeps the permissions it had.

### Workaround

Over the daemon's control socket, `turn/start` with `sandboxPolicy: {type: "dangerFullAccess"}` and `approvalPolicy: "never"` restores the previous behavior for that turn and subsequent turns.

### Versions

codex-cli 0.160.1, app-server 0.160.1 (updated from 0.160.0 by the managed daemon), macOS 26.6.2 arm64.

15: {"id": "codex-51279", "titulo": "ChatGPT Web: pinned project folders are omitted from the Projects interface", "texto": "## Summary

On **ChatGPT Web**, a project folder that has been pinned can disappear from the **Projects** tab/interface instead of remaining visible in the complete projects list.

The project itself still exists and remains accessible through **Pinned**. The problem is the Projects interface no longer shows that same project once it is pinned.

Pinning should be a presentation/priority state, not a filter that removes the project from the canonical project browser.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open ChatGPT Web.
2. Create or use an existing ChatGPT Project.
3. Pin that project.
4. Confirm it appears in the **Pinned** section.
5. Open the **Projects** tab/interface.
6. Observe that the pinned project is missing from the Projects list.

## Expected behavior

The **Projects** interface should show all accessible projects, regardless of pin state.

A pinned project should therefore:

- remain visible in **Projects**;
- also appear in **Pinned** as a shortcut/high-priority item;
- keep the same project identity and contents in both representations;
- not require unpinning just to make it visible in the Projects browser again.

Pinning should affect prominence/order, not membership in the project catalog.

## Actual behavior

After a project is pinned, it is omitted from the **Projects** tab/interface.

This makes **Pinned** and **Projects** behave like mutually exclusive buckets even though pinning is only an organizational state.

## Why this matters

The Projects tab should be the canonical place to browse the user's projects. If pinned projects are filtered out:

- the Projects view is incomplete;
- users can reasonably think projects are missing or deleted;
- project discoverability depends on remembering pin state;
- a navigation preference unexpectedly changes catalog visibility.

16: {"id": "codex-51293", "titulo": "Codex exec fails during in-process app-server initialization with read-only CODEX_HOME", "texto": "Running Codex CLI inside a ChatGPT-managed cloud development container fails during startup with:

“failed to initialize in-process app-server client: Read-only file system (os error 30)”

The command exits with status 1 without returning the requested “OK”. The problem persists after rebuilding the environment. I have not established whether nested Codex CLI execution is supported here or whether this is a regression.

Environment:
- Codex CLI 0.159.0-alpha.3 at /opt/codex/bin/codex
- CODEX_HOME=/run/codex-environment/codex-home, readable but read-only
- Project directory is writable
- Login status reports “Logged in using ChatGPT”

Test:
A single codex exec invocation was launched in an empty temporary directory, using the existing ChatGPT authentication, --sandbox read-only, --ephemeral, --ignore-user-config and --ignore-rules. The prompt requested only “OK”; no research simulation was run. The outer command was not retried. Internal network-request count is unknown.

Observed diagnostics:
- A PATH-alias initialization warning also reports a read-only filesystem
- installation_id is absent from CODEX_HOME
- A temporary-file write probe there fails with EROFS
- A SQLite initialization probe fails with SQLITE_CANTOPEN, not SQLITE_READONLY
- These probes do not identify the exact write operation causing the app-server initialization failure

Questions:
1. Is nested Codex CLI execution supported in this managed environment?
2. Which paths must be writable for initialization, including with --ephemeral?
3. Is there an officially supported way to separate writable runtime state from the managed read-only CODEX_HOME?
4. Could the error report the failing path or operation?"}

macOS (Darwin arm64)

N/A (hook behavior, model-independent)

### Codex doctor report
Not relevant to this issue.

### What issue are you seeing?
When a review is started from the TUI with `/review`, the review finishes (the TUI shows the result and the rollout records `task_complete`), but no `Stop` hook is dispatched, and no `SubagentStop` either. A regular prompt turn dispatches `Stop` when it ends.

The rollout for a `/review` shows, in order: `task_complete` for the review thread, the `ExitedReviewMode` item, then `task_complete` for the parent turn. No `Stop` hook is dispatched for either completion.

167: {"id": "codex-53360", "titulo": "Codex Desktop: Show active Git branch prominently above the chat composer to prevent wrong-branch edits", "texto": "## Summary

Add a **persistent, highly visible indicator of the active Git branch immediately above or beside the chat input** in Codex Desktop, so users can confirm the target branch **before sending instructions**.

## Problem

When switching between projects, threads, worktrees, or Git branches, it's easy to lose track of the branch the current conversation is operating on. This can lead to asking Codex to edit code in the wrong branch. The most important moment to confirm this context is **right before sending a prompt**, not after the agent has started working.

## Proposed UX

Show a prominent but compact badge near the message composer, for example:

**Current branch: ⑂ `feature/login`**

The indicator should be readable at a glance without opening menus or hovering. Placement is flexible, as long as it stays visible while composing a message.

## Expected behavior / acceptance criteria

- The active Git branch is clearly visible while composing a message, with no extra clicks.
- The displayed branch reflects the **actual checked-out branch in the current conversation's working tree**, not the repository's default branch or a stale selection.
- The indicator updates promptly on thread, project, worktree, or branch changes.
- When no branch exists (such as detached HEAD), or the branch cannot be determined, show an explicit state rather than a misleading branch name.
- A recognizable Git branch icon and legible, high-contrast label make the context easy to recognize.

## Why this matters

168: {"id": "codex-53435", "titulo": "Feature Request: Show Authenticated ChatGPT Account in Codex CLI", "texto": "### What variant of Codex are you using?

This is a basic but important feature for developers working across personal and enterprise environments.

171: {"id": "codex-53461", "titulo": "Backend ends HTTP Responses streams at ~900 s and closes websocket turns (1000/1012) before response.completed on long gpt-6.1-sol reasoning turns", "texto": "### What issue are you seeing?

The client sees a clean TLS/TCP close mid-body (`h11 RemoteProtocolError: peer closed connection without sending complete message body (incomplete chunked read)`); no `error` frame arrives first. Turns that finish under 15 minutes complete normally; turns that need more than 15 minutes can never complete, because each retry re-runs the full generation and hits the same wall. 197: {"id": "codex-53835", "titulo": "[CLI] `codex agents` checks launch-directory trust before opening the overview", "texto": "## Summary

198: {"id": "codex-53836", "titulo": "[TUI] Resumed in-progress turns reset the elapsed-time indicator", "texto": "## Summary

When the TUI resumes a session whose latest turn is still in progress, the status indicator appears to restart its elapsed timer instead of reflecting the turn's original start time. The status can therefore show approximately `0s` even when the turn has been running much longer.

## Source trace

The replay path receives `started_at` for each turn, but the `TurnStatus::InProgress` branch calls `on_task_started()` without passing or restoring that timestamp. `on_task_started()` resets the status timer to zero. The live start notification and replay path therefore use different timing information.

## Expected behavior

For a replayed in-progress turn with a start timestamp, initialize the status timer from that timestamp so the elapsed indicator continues across reconnect/resume. Keep the zero-time behavior for a genuinely new live turn.

## Reproduction

1. Start a turn and leave it running long enough for the status indicator to show elapsed time.
2. Reopen or resume that thread in the TUI while the turn remains active.
3. Observe that the status timer starts near zero rather than showing the elapsed duration.

This is a TUI replay/status issue, separate from thread ownership or active-writer locking."}

213: {"id": "codex-54127", "titulo": "codex-arg0: reuse inherited PATH aliases when CODEX_HOME is read-only inside sandboxed sub-processes", "texto": "## Summary
When `codex` (or a `codex` test binary / child CLI sub-process) runs inside a `workspace-write` or `read-only` sandbox where `CODEX_HOME` (`~/.codex`) is outside the writable roots, `arg0_dispatch()` attempts to create a new temporary directory under `~/.codex/tmp/arg0` and call `chmod(0o700)` on `~/.codex/tmp/arg0`. This fails with `EPERM`/`EACCES` (`PermissionDenied`) or `EROFS` (`ReadOnlyFilesystem`), printing:

```text
WARNING: proceeding, even though we could not create PATH aliases: Operation not permitted (os error 1)
```

As a result, `Arg0PathEntryGuard` is `None`, and `main_execve_wrapper_exe` / `codex_linux_sandbox_exe` are dropped even when a parent `codex` process has already created and locked a valid `codex-arg0*` alias directory under `~/.codex/tmp/arg0` and passed it via `PATH`.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start a parent `codex` session (which creates `~/.codex/tmp/arg0/codex-arg0...` and prepends it to `PATH`).
2. Inside a `workspace-write` sandbox where `~/.codex` is read-only, invoke a child `codex` sub-process (for example `codex --version` or a `codex-core` test).

249: {"id": "codex-54599", "titulo": "`$HOME/.codex` is loaded as a project config layer when `CODEX_HOME` points somewhere else (follow-up to #9932)", "texto": "### What version of Codex is running?

codex-cli 0.163.0, the latest release. Also reproduced on 0.160.1. Current `main` has the same check.

### What platform is your computer?

### What issue are you seeing?

Run Codex with `CODEX_HOME` set to a directory other than `$HOME/.codex`, and with the working directory at `$HOME`. The default home folder `$HOME/.codex` is then discovered as a **project** `.codex` layer.

The project root falls back to cwd when no `.git` marker is found. If `$HOME` is a trusted project, the whole `config.toml` of that other home applies to the session, and it applies with project precedence, above the active user config. That covers:

- model, approval and personality settings;
- MCP servers;
- hooks from `$HOME/.codex/hooks.json`;
- skills under `$HOME/.codex/skills`;
- plugin enablement;
- marketplace sources and MCP env values that point into the other home's directories.

If `$HOME` is not trusted, you get the "config folders are disabled" warning from #9932 instead.

Seen through the app-server, `config/read` with `{"cwd": "<HOME>", "includeLayers": true}` lists `{"type": "project", "dotCodexFolder": "<HOME>/.codex"}` above the `user` layer for `<CODEX_HOME>/config.toml`. The `origins` show the project layer winning keys that the active home also sets.

PR #10207 fixed #9932 by skipping a discovered `.codex` folder only when it **is** the active `CODEX_HOME`. Here is the check in `codex-rs/config/src/loader/mod.rs`, in the project-layer discovery loop:

```rust
if dot_codex_abs == codex_home_abs || dot_codex_normalized == codex_home_normalized {
    continue;
}
```

When `CODEX_HOME` is a different directory, `$HOME/.codex` no longer matches, and it is treated as an ordinary project folder.
